scope: Daily UI/UX, application repair identity, permission visibility, recovery and editing controls

checks: Unicode paste, 3–8-row composer and draft preservation across resize/modals
Model catalog, search, pagination, no-result state and mode selection
Ctrl+U edits the draft; Task and Context open and close
Literal argument editor exposes the end of long paths
LSP approval shows command and target before the probe starts
No raw noisy LSP stderr on terminal
Factual project explanation with source citation; repairs remain in process details
Exact command does not start before UI approval
Live output appears before exit and human input reaches the PTY
Queued instruction is persisted after the tool result
Idle composer returns after completion without a repeated command

development_failures_resolved: Temporary filesystem quota: use workspace build cache and temporary directory.
Harness synchronization: wait for panel dismissal before sending the next command.
Long fixture paths: inspect the literal argument editor instead of assuming an untruncated form.
Test markers counted as unvalidated source changes: move only instrumentation to the existing derived-cache area; preserve completion guard and all source comparisons.
limitations: A local PTY fixture is not a comparative quality or latency benchmark.
The noisy LSP is a controlled fixture, not every real language server.
Desktop notification delivery is covered through routing tests, not visual desktop acceptance.
Legacy repair messages without origin metadata are not hidden by text heuristics.
Prose width applies to prose-only messages; messages with fenced code or tables retain terminal width.
The test-specific context limit is never saved to the user configuration.
